tables.native_tps_release_late_cc3_evidence: At 3000 RPM and two-step ADC0/6 release, original S88 supplied only G 7580h and 7581h MOVC returns matches G in the first 200 captured CC3 schedules but has 364 versus 363 modeled pulse starts. A capture from tick 2500000 exposes one later mismatch at tick 3560295: G IRAM14h:15h=0000h, S88 donor=00CFh. Prior PC1EA9h candidates are 00C8h and 00CFh against the shared strict ROM7218h:7219h=00C8h bound. Supplying G values at all 14 reached 7B46h MOVC cells removes the mismatch, matches all 152 late captured schedules and 363 starts, and changes final RAM69h from 67h to G's 5Fh. G 7B45h=05h does not remove it. P5.0 width histograms still differ; physical connection of modeled CPU P1.3/CC3 is unverified. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/s88_native_3000_g7580_g7581_{late_math_window,g7b46,g7b45}/; test: NativeCalibrationPairTests.test_7b46_closes_one_late_cc3_difference_at_3000_rpm.
tables.native_tps_release_two_cell_isolation: In the same 3000 RPM S88 run with G 7580h/7581h MOVC returns, the reached 7B46h matrix cells 7B4Fh (row 0, column 9, S88=68h/G=60h) and 7B5Eh (row 1, column 9, S88=63h/G=5Bh) each occur 132 times. Supplying only G 7B4Fh changes final IRAM69h 67h->62h but leaves the late 1EA9h candidate 00CFh and 364 modeled CC3 starts; only G 7B5Eh gives IRAM69h=64h with the same candidate and starts. Supplying both gives IRAM69h=5Fh, candidate 00C8h, zero late schedule and 363 starts, exactly matching all 152 late G CC3-entry values. Four frequently read cells at 7BA9h/7BAAh/7BB8h/7BB9h and the other six reached cells do not suffice in this state. This isolates a joint digital effect; the exact mediation from matrix interpolation to the CC3 gate and physical wiring remain unknown. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/s88_native_3000_{7b4f_only,7b5e_only,7b46_lower,7b46_hot,7b46_rest}/; test: NativeCalibrationPairTests.test_7b46_closes_one_late_cc3_difference_at_3000_rpm.
tables.timer0_7a_read_race_mediation: Original Fiat opcodes at 1CD4h read IRAM7Ah for MUL AB; Timer 0 vector 000Bh reaches writer 07B3h. In the 3000 RPM native TPS-release event, G reads 7Ah=8Dh at tick 3551892 before 07B3h writes 85h at 3551998, while S88 with G 7580h/7581h MOVC donations reads 85h at 3552010 after that write at 3551997. G 7B4Fh+7B5Eh donations move S88 read before the write. At 1CDFh G/dual-cell S88 A:B=C5:0D versus S88 partial donor FD:0C; subsequent F8:08h=72h versus 73h and PC1EA9h candidate 00C8h versus 00CFh cross the shared strict 00C8h bound. A time-gated override only of the 1CD4h IRAM read is reciprocal: give S88 8Dh and its late schedule becomes zero; give G 85h and it becomes 00CFh. Stored IRAM7Ah and original ROM bytes are preserved by this override. This establishes an emulated interrupt/read ordering mediator in this state; upstream cause of the timing shift and physical P1.3/CC3 connection remain open. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/{g_native_3000_race,s88_native_3000_race,s88_native_3000_race_lower,g_native_3000_7a85_read_window,s88_native_3000_7a8d_read}/; test: NativeCalibrationPairTests.test_7a_read_order_mediates_late_cc3_gate.
tables.timer0_7a_pc_window: Bounded pre-instruction PC traces at ticks 3551850..3552025 localize preemption. G and S88 with G 7B4Fh+7B5Eh returns pass PC1CB7h at 3551873, read RAM7Ah at PC1CD4h at 3551892, and enter Timer0 vector 000Bh at 3551897. S88 with only G 7580h+7581h returns passes PC1CB7h at 3551877, enters vector 000Bh at 3551896 while at PC1CCFh, and reads RAM7Ah at PC1CD4h at 3552010 after ISR return. The source of the four-tick foreground phase difference before PC1CB7h is unresolved. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/{g_pcwindow,s88_pcwindow,s88_lower_pcwindow}/.
tables.timer0_7a_prephase_window: In the earlier ticks 3550900..3551900, G and S88 with both G matrix cells have identical PCs at all 1001 ticks. S88 with only G 7580h+7581h returns is shifted by four ticks over most of this range. The phase source precedes this window. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/{g_prephase,s88_prephase,s88_lower_prephase}/.
tables.timer0_7a_phase_limit: At ticks 3274000..3275000, G and S88 with both G matrix cells have identical PCs at all 1001 ticks; the S88 partial donor mostly aligns with G at a two-tick shift in the opposite direction to the later four-tick shift near 3551892. Thus the relative phase evolves across execution and is not a fixed per-cell latency. At ticks 2500000..2501000 the same three runs do not exhibit a single stable alignment, so the late event cannot be extrapolated to all operating states. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/{g_release_pc,s88_release_pc,s88_lower_release_pc,g_high_pc,s88_high_pc,s88_lower_high_pc}/.
tables.timer0_7a_prior_interrupt_phase: An earlier Timer0 event exposes already different caller stages. Original G code enables ET0 at PC0578h; pending Timer0 enters vector 000Bh with PC057Ah next, before completing that RET. After ISR, execution revisits PC057Ah and returns to its caller. G and S88 with both G 7B4Fh/7B5Eh cells enter the vector at tick 3510947, reach RAM7Ah writer 07B3h at 3511055, and resume PC1CA5h at 3511068. S88 with only G 7580h/7581h enters the vector at 3510949, reaches writer at 3511057, and resumes PC5225h at 3511070, still inside the multiply helper called at PC1C9Dh; it executes PC5227h and PC1CA0h..1CA4h before reaching PC1CA5h at 3511077. The Timer0 event reveals different caller return addresses; it does not itself establish the source of their earlier phase difference. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/{g_7a_prev_pc,s88_7a_prev_pc,s88_lower_7a_prev_pc}/.
tables.adc2_2000_selector_evidence: With G code, 2000 RPM, raw ADC0/3/5/6/7=180/40/40/247/63 and 2.4M ticks, changing only ADC2 40->220 changes 7B46h..7BBDh MOVC reads from 6 startup reads to 918 reads while 7CAEh..7D25h changes 912->0. tables.visual_evidence: Original-ROM 8x15 G/S88: the first 117 S88 cells equal G+8, while the last three (row 7, columns 12-14) are unchanged. In S37/S36, the first 116 cells equal G+22 and the last four (row 7, columns 11-14) are unchanged. The within-S88 7D26h/7D9Eh comparison differs at seven last-column cells already different in G and three terminal cells preserved only in 7D9Eh. Verified by MatrixPlotTests.test_7d9e_variant_offsets_preserve_terminal_cells. Physical axis scale and natural mode-2 reachability remain unknown.
tables.static_evidence: All six 70BAh words point to 7D9Eh. Identical G 5228h and A 52EBh loaders use RAM57h*2 as a pointer-directory offset; G 334Dh and A 3369h can supply base 70B6h.
tables.dynamic_evidence: Isolated original-ROM G/A/S37/S88 execution selects base 70B6h, sets RAM57h=2, R5=4 and T2CON.1=0, then reaches MOVC at 532Fh/53F2h with DPTR=7D9Eh. ROM[7DA2h] becomes R2 and upper IRAM A4h: 77h in G/A, 8Dh in S37, 7Fh in S88. Natural G execution at ADC0=180, ADC6=247, ADC2=100, ADC3=80, ADC7=63 reaches the 2Fh.2 guard but remains at RAM57h=0 and reads 7CAEh. Forcing only RAM57h=2 before 1378h makes the original G ROM read 7D9Eh; the firmware later clears 57h at 3B94h. Mode 2 is an intervention, not demonstrated as a natural operating state.
tables.controlled_full_run_evidence: With forced RAM57h=2 and 2.4M ticks, G at 750/1000/1500 RPM makes 912/494/480 MOVC reads in 7D9Eh..7E15h. Substituting only S88's 120 matrix bytes changes upper IRAM A4h, IRAM69h and reload RAM34h in all three cases; P5.0/P5.1 low-width medians change 6017->6094, 5910->5910 and 5260->5234 ticks respectively. Active G ROM SHA is unchanged. The selector also affects other lookups, so the forced-mode width relative to natural mode 0 cannot be attributed solely to 7D9Eh; the within-mode donor contrast isolates this matrix.

tables.output: Selected byte is written to upper IRAM[8Dh] and consumed by the 37C9h/37DFh countdown in G/S88; physical role unverified
tables.static_evidence: All six ROMs hold 70D4h→7E8Eh and identical 15 nominal bytes. G 37B9h copies ACC.7 to carry, masks ACC to its low nibble, adds carry, then MOVC at 37BFh. Index 15 or 16 reaches the next pointer interval at 7E9Dh or 7E9Eh; natural reachability of these indices is unknown.
tables.dynamic_evidence: Historical tps_gate63_40_95_g/s88 captures contain PC37BFh reads at 7E91h=01h and 7E93h=02h, but lack an emulator executable hash. Current-executable G/S88 controls (SHA 1c0b13f3...28804) at 1000 RPM, raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63 and 3.4M ticks read neither 7E8Eh nor upper IRAM8Dh; historical steady-TPS access is not revalidated. In the current experimental P4.6-low double-TPS-step scenario, G/S88 each read 7E8Eh once; G reads 7E93h=02h and S88 7E95h=03h. Isolated original-opcode execution in all six ROMs confirms the index formula and upper IRAM8Dh write for BC=03h,05h,07h,8Ah,8Fh. BC=8Fh exercises index 16 only as a boundary test, not an observed full-boot state.
tables.countdown_consumer_evidence: Original G/S88 opcodes at 377Fh and 37C9h read upper IRAM 8Dh through CJNE @R1,#00h (R1=8Dh), and 37DFh decrements the same byte with DEC @R1. In matched 1500-RPM runs with experimental P4.6 low and two ADC0/6 steps, the original G and S88 7E8Eh table bytes are identical, yet G PC37BFh reads 7E93h=02h once and S88 reads 7E95h=03h once; PC37C3h stores that value in upper 8Dh. G then reads 02h,01h,00h at PC37C9h and S88 reads 03h,02h,01h,00h; every positive value is read again by DEC @R1 at 37DFh. This proves an extra digital countdown passage from a changed index, not a physical time scale or output effect. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/upper8d_read_probe_{g,s88}_tps/.
tables.single_byte_causal_evidence: With original G ROM, identical inputs and current emulator hash 1c0b13f3...28804, replacing only the MOVC return at PC37BFh/7E93h from 02h to 03h changes upper IRAM8Dh countdown from 02,01,00 to 03,02,01,00. The P5.0 summary is identical; one modeled P5.1 low width shifts 1769→1768 ticks while its median stays 1784 and CC3 pin-model median stays 5881. This is a digital control-flow and one-tick timing observation, not a proven physical calibration effect. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/upper8d_read_probe_g_tps/ and upper8d_g_override_03/.
tables.visual_evidence: tools/plot_ma17_state_curve.py plots the common six-ROM 15-byte raw staircase in build/ma17-analysis/variants/matrix_plots/curve_7e8e_all_variants.png and exports per-cell CSV/JSON with ROM hashes; observed G/S88 lookup indices 5/7 are annotated without assigning a physical axis.

tables.three_gate_counterexample: Original G ROM at 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=40/95 stepped to 180/247 at tick 200000, ADC2/3/7=100/80/63, with RAM78=80h supplied only at PC1D4Bh: 62 visits to PC3752h include 41 with both IRAM21h.1 and 2Fh.7 set. The path reaches PC37FBh 166 times, but B.0 is clear at every captured visit; code at 37E3h then clears F0 and selects the 7300h+60h alternative, bypassing the 70CEh/7E16h lookup. No 7E16h MOVC reads occur in 2.4M ticks. This intervention proves the two flags alone are insufficient in this state; it does not establish natural reachability or physical purpose. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_tps_step_ram78/; test: VariantTraceTests.test_7e16_path_needs_state_bit_even_when_two_flags_overlap.
tables.b0_provenance: G 36AFh loads B from upper IRAM81h; at 36DEh B.5 selects the 36ECh/3701h path that ORs B with 05h and can retain B.0. G 2D85h enters 2DC8h on a prior 2Fh.0=1/current 2Fh.0=0 transition; 2E06h then can OR 24h into upper IRAM81h when ROM[72A6h]+IRAM46h is below IRAM47h without carry and XRAM low F9h=0. ROM[72A6h]=06h and ROM[72DEh]=96h in all six images. In the stepped G trace, 231 captured 36DEh visits all have B.5=0; neither 3701h nor 371Dh is reached. Forcing P4.6 low from tick 200000 reaches 2D85h but not 2DC8h/2E06h in 2.4M ticks. These are code conditions and negative emulation observations, not a demonstrated natural producer chain. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_b_source/ and 7e16_p46_low_step/.
tables.isolated_b0_producer_evidence: Original G opcodes from 2E06h with IRAM46h=40h, IRAM47h=48h and XRAM F8F9h=0 read ROM72A6h=06h, write ROM72DEh=96h to F8FAh and set upper IRAM81h=24h. Equal IRAM47h=46h or F8F9h=1 blocks both writes. The original 36AFh/36B1h instructions load B from upper81h; with F8FAh=FFh prepared, 36DEh reaches 3701h and sets B.0, while blocked controls reach 3739h. This is isolated execution with a deliberate PC transition and prepared F8FAh, not natural boot reachability or a 7E16h lookup.
tables.full_boot_experimental_b0_evidence: G original ROM with experimental P4.6 low and ADC6 raw 95->220 at tick 200000 executes 2DC8h/2E06h in 2.4M ticks. At 1000 RPM, IRAM46h=2Ah and IRAM47h=28h fail the ROM72A6h=06h comparison. At 1500 RPM, IRAM47h=3Ch passes, original 2E1Ch writes F8FAh=96h and B.5 appears at 36DEh. No 7E16h read follows: ROM72D6h=02h, upper IRAM C5h=53h and lower IRAM70h=53h leave carry clear at 36FFh, routing to 3739h. This establishes a digital full-boot path under an experimental port stimulus, not natural wiring or physical calibration purpose. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_p46_low_tps_fault_step_probe/ and 7e16_rpm_1500_branch_probe/.
tables.double_tps_step_reachability: Original G and S88 ROMs, 1500 RPM, ADC0/6 initially 40/95, ADC6->220 at tick 200000 then ADC0/6->180/247 at tick 1350000, experimental P4.6 low, no RAM or MOVC override: upper C5h stays 53h while lower 70h rises to DFh; carry at G 36FFh routes through 3701h. Both execute PC3830h 80 times and read four 7E16h cells 80 times each (320 MOVC reads). G reads 7E66h/7E67h/7E75h/7E76h; S88 reads 7E76h/7E77h/7E85h/7E86h although their full 120-byte 7E16h tables are identical. Paired PC3830h->384Ch upper-CAh outputs: G 00h:37,01h:18,02h:19,03h:6; S88 00h:18,01h:10,02h:11,03h:10,04h:12,05h:19. Removing P4.6-low or the first TPS step gives zero 7E16h reads in 3.4M ticks. This proves state-dependent digital selection in the emulated Fiat hardware profile, not P4.6 wiring or a physical calibration unit. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_double_tps_step_no_ram78_uca/, 7e16_double_tps_step_s88/, 7e16_double_tps_step_p46_default/, 7e16_single_tps_step_p46_low/.
tables.two_calibration_selector_evidence: At the same experimental P4.6-low double-TPS step, original G has upper BCh=05h, lower 68h=B5h and R5=50h on all 80 PC3830h entries; original S88 has BCh=96h, 68h=86h and R5=60h. Supplying S88 ROM7580h=25h only as G MOVC return gives BCh=96h, 68h=C5h and R5=51h; its four 7E16h reads move one column to 7E67h/7E68h/7E76h/7E77h. Supplying both S88 7580h=25h and S88's original 225-byte 7581h matrix via pointer-verified MOVC donation makes G's 80 ordered (BCh,68h,R5,R1,upper CAh) pairs identical to native S88 and reads the same four 7E16h cells 80 times each. The active G ROM SHA stays original; donor S88 SHA is recorded. This proves sufficiency for these selected digital events, not whole-ECU equivalence or physical units. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_index_trace_{g,s88}/, 7e16_index_g_7580s88/, 7e16_index_g_7580_7581_donor_s88/.
tables.upper_ca_consumer_clamp_evidence: G/S88 original-ROM full-boot traces with the experimental P4.6-low double-TPS step reach upper-CAh reader PC39B2h 79 times after tick 1400000. G CAh varies 00h..03h, S88 00h..05h, but upper C8h and B stay 05h; CAh never wins the maximum. At 78 completed PC39F4h visits, (R2,B,A) is always (97h,05h,9Ch) for G or (99h,05h,9Eh) for S88. PC3A48h is visited twice after the second step with CAh=00h. This shows a consumed but masked matrix result in this state; different P5/CC3 widths between ROMs cannot be assigned to 7E16h from these observations. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_ca_consumer_{g,s88}/; test: Matrix7e16ReachabilityTests.test_double_tps_step_selects_same_table_at_different_cells.
tables.alcohol_table_donor_full_boot: Original G ROM under the experimental P4.6-low double-TPS step, with only 120 original A ROM bytes 7E16h..7E8Dh supplied at the pointer-verified MOVC return, executes 80 lookups at the same four ROM addresses as the G control. The raw MOVC trace and active G ROM hash stay original; effective interpolated R3 changes 38h->52h on all 80 PC384Ch samples. Upper CAh differs in 54 of 80 ordered writes, ranging 00h..05h instead of 00h..03h. After tick 1400000, upper CAh never exceeds B=05h at PC39B2h; all 78 completed PC39F4h visits keep (R2,B,A)=(97h,05h,9Ch) and modeled P5.0/P5.1 and CC3 median low widths match the control. This isolates a digital calibration effect and its clamp in the tested G-code state, not natural behavior of A code or equivalence of all pin edges. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_g_matched/, 7e16_a_donor_g/; test: Matrix7e16ReachabilityTests.test_alcohol_matrix_donor_changes_upper_ca_but_is_clamped.
tables.adc2_clamp_crossing: Changing only raw ADC2 from 100 to 200 in the same G-code P4.6-low double-TPS scenario preserves 320 MOVC reads of 7E16h. With ADC2=200, upper CAh changes in 54/80 ordered writes under the original A-table MOVC donation. Upper C9h/CBh and B are 00h at 78 post-tick-1400000 PC39B2h visits, allowing CAh through; at PC39F4h input R2=9Ch and A=9Ch+CAh. Modeled P5.1 median low width changes 1775->1784 ticks, while P5.0 stays 1782 and CC3 stays 6373; physical pin assignment and R2-to-P5.1 mediation are unproven. At ADC2=50, B=0Bh and CAh<=05h is masked. Active ROM SHA remains G, donor SHA is A. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_g_adc2_200/, 7e16_a_donor_adc2_{50,200}/; test: Matrix7e16ReachabilityTests.test_alcohol_matrix_reaches_r2_when_adc2_lowers_clamp.
tables.upper_ca_crossed_mediation: At raw ADC2=200, crossing original G table versus A MOVC table donation with MA17_ZERO_UPPER_CA_AT_39B2=1 preserves all 80 matrix lookups and 54/80 differences in pre-consumer upper-CAh writes. The intervention makes PC39B2h read CAh=00h and PC39F4h calculate A=9Ch in both arms. With the zero applied, structured output-latch, CC3, CC3/P5 phase, engine-RAM-change and PC-coverage reports match exactly; P5.0/P5.1 median low widths are both 1767 ticks. Without the zero, P5.1 medians differ 1775/1784. Thus the modeled difference depends on upper CAh at this consumer. The precise later branch and physical wiring remain unknown. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_{g,a_donor}_adc2_200_ca_zero/; test: Matrix7e16ReachabilityTests.test_alcohol_matrix_reaches_r2_when_adc2_lowers_clamp.
tables.ram69_timer1_median_mediation: At ADC2=200, G original code with its own versus A-donor 7E16h table reaches PC3B06h 78 times after tick 1400000. The value A and upper IRAM8Ch at the write span 9Ch..9Fh for G and 9Ch..A1h with the donor; observed lower IRAM69h transient writes reach 9Fh versus A1h, although both final values are 9Ch. G PC043Bh reads IRAM69h in the Timer 1 reload path. Crossing the two tables with MA17_OVERRIDE_RAM69=9C only at this read preserves different PC3B06h producer writes but equalizes observed 34h/35h reload writes and P5.0/P5.1 median low widths to 1767 ticks; CC3 median remains 6373. The P5.1 width histograms are not identical, so this establishes mediation of the modeled median only, not every edge. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_{g,a_donor}_adc2_200_ram69_path/ and 7e16_{g,a_donor}_adc2_200_ram69_9c/; test: Matrix7e16ReachabilityTests.test_alcohol_matrix_reaches_r2_when_adc2_lowers_clamp.
tables.isolated_upper_ca_consumer_test: Original G opcodes at 39B2h..39F4h with controlled R2=10h, R7=7Fh and B=05h yield R2=15h for upper CAh=03h or 05h, but R2=18h for CAh=08h. Homologous A opcodes at 39E0h..3A22h yield R2=27h/41h for CAh=17h/31h, the values from the separate isolated 7E16h lookup. This confirms the maximum and additive path in isolated execution; it does not establish full-boot reachability in A, whose dynamic hardware profile is not yet validated. Test: Sab80C517.FiatAndAlcoholUpperCaConsumerUsesMaximumBeforeUpdatingR2.
tables.adc2_716c_clamp_interaction: With original G code at raw ADC2=122, C8h=B=01h on 78 post-tick-1400000 PC39B2h visits. G table versus original A-table MOVC donation changes the count where CAh exceeds B from 25 to 43 and modeled P5.1 median low width from 1802.5 to 1793.5 ticks. At ADC2=123, C8h=B=00h, the counts are 43 versus 54 and both P5.1 medians are 1784 ticks. CC3 median remains 5969 in all four arms. These matched interventions show an internal matrix effect on both sides of the clamp boundary but no monotonic median response. Active G and A donor ROM hashes are checked; neither physical output nor ADC2 sensor identity is established. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/7e16_adc2_cc_donor_{122,123}/; test: tests.test_ma17_adc2_716c_gate.
tables.upstream_ae_evidence: At G/S88 PC330Dh after tick 1500000, 68 stable upper-AEh samples are 43h in native G, 44h in G receiving only S88 ROM7580h=25h, and 4Ch in both G receiving S88 7580h plus the 7581h matrix donor and native S88. tables.visual_evidence: All 60 cells in original A and A+ equal min(255, G+34) at the same 7ED9h matrix index. The 7ED9h G/A heatmap preserves the raw silhouette with an expanded saturation plateau. This is an exact byte relation, not a physical scale or a matched operating point; A/A+ use upper AFh rather than G's 7Dh for the row axis. Verified by MatrixPlotTests.test_alcohol_7ed9_and_7f51_are_saturated_byte_shifts.
tables.static_evidence: G 3291h computes R5=second_segment_index*first_axis_count+first_segment_index; first-axis count=0Ah, second count=06h; 5349h adds R0=0Ah for next-row reads. A/A+/S37/S36 share identical code at 3295h..32D7h, 52EBh..5308h, 533Ch..53A8h and 53E6h..5429h; 32ADh uses the same 10-byte row stride and 52EBh selects big-endian table pointer by RAM57h. The second-axis header byte differs: AFh in A/A+ versus 7Dh in S37/S36.
tables.isolated_A_code_evidence: With original ROM code 32ADh..32D5h, IRAM47h=28h, RAM57h=0 and selected second-axis value 20h, IRAM31h becomes 9Ah in A (upper AFh axis) and 78h in S37 (lower 7Dh axis). No complete A/S37 boot or hardware profile was used.
tables.isolated_A_S37_timer1_bound: Continuing original A/S37 code at 043Bh..0521h after those isolated 31h outputs, with identical RAM36h:37h=011Dh and a sweep of RAM69h=00h..FFh, first separates calculated RAM34h:35h at RAM69h=12h: A=FFFFh, S37=12FEh. Within RAM69h=80h..A5h, all 20 values 80h..93h separate the reloads and 94h..A5h converge. At RAM69h=FFh both converge to C0FEh despite 22h.7=0/1. Consumer opcodes 043Bh..0521h are identical in both ROMs; crossing only post-lookup RAM31h at RAM69h=12h or 89h swaps the reload values. This confirms local RAM31h mediation in synthetic states, not natural reachability, physical output identity, or a full-ROM A/S37 timing contrast.
tables.ram69_reachability_constraint: A shared original producer can output RAM69h=80h when flag 2Bh.4 is set, within the isolated A/S37 Timer1-discriminating interval 80h..93h. The serial-state R2=38h branch can set that flag at lower RAM47h<=64h in isolated six-ROM execution, but a real protocol session and coexistence with the associated matrix/producer states have not been shown in A/S37; no full-ROM timing difference is claimed.
tables.dynamic_evidence: At 1000 RPM/ADC1=40, MOVC reads offsets 03h/04h and 0Dh/0Eh via PCs 532Fh/5333h/534Bh/5350h; 836 reads in 2.2 s. With corrected C517A ADC, 1000 RPM/ADC7=63 and 2.4M ticks, substituting only returned MOVC bytes of G/S88 7ED9h..7F14h with the original A table changes IRAM31h 10h->32h and P5.0 low medians G 1861->5792, S88 1921->5852 ticks while CC3 scheduling median stays 1422. Active ROM hashes and raw MOVC values remain original; A code was not executed.
tables.ram31_mediation_evidence: In original G code at 1000 RPM, ADC7=63 and 2.4M ticks, MOVC table G/A yields natural IRAM31h=10h/32h. Forcing only IRAM31h immediately before the Timer 1 MOV direct,direct at PC0490 gives a crossed P5.0/P5.1 low-width result: G table/31h=10h ->1861 ticks; G table/forced 32h ->5792; A donor table/31h=32h ->5792; A donor table/forced 10h ->1861. The active ROM remains G; A code is not executed. This demonstrates full mediation in the tested emulated state, not physical coil wiring.
tables.ram31_mediation_rpm_extension: The PC0490 RAM31 probe originally had an early return unless IRAM47h=28h; it now accepts any nonzero RPM byte and logs the actual value. With the G ROM active and ADC7=63, at 750 RPM (47h=1Eh) G/A MOVC tables give natural 31h=0Ch/2Eh and P5.0/P5.1 widths 1940/7181 ticks; forcing the opposite 31h swaps the widths exactly. At 2000 RPM (47h=50h), 31h=1Fh/41h and widths 1789/3769 ticks, again swapped exactly by the crossed override. P5 periods remain 79200/29700 ticks. All cases use original G ROM bytes and execute G code only.
tables.ram31_scale_evidence: G 0490h..049Bh loads B=31h, computes A=(69h>>1)-B with carry cleared, then 04A0h replaces B by 1Eh and 04A3h multiplies A*B. At 1000 RPM and stabilized RAM69h=9Ah, forced 31h=10h/32h gives pre-049Bh A=3Dh/1Bh while carry remains equal. P5 median period=59400 ticks; forced 31h=00h/10h/20h/32h/40h/50h/80h gives modeled low widths 989/1861/3725/5792/7424/9286/14849 ticks. For nonzero sampled values, period*31h/512 fits within 12.5 ticks; at zero a 989-tick floor appears, and at 750 RPM the simple approximation errs by up to 84 ticks. This is a local empirical fit, not an exact fixed-point decoding or physical dwell measurement.

tables.rpm1500_adc3_reti_window: A 61-tick PC window at the first ADC3 step shows G, S88 and G+7580h donor execute the same Timer-0 ISR ADC-service path through RETI at 084Fh/tick 901852. At tick 901853 they resume foreground at 5246h, 4697h and 468Eh respectively. S88 and the donor then restore old upper IRAM A8h before publishing the new ADC3 value in 63h, whereas native G publishes it earlier. This identifies interrupt/foreground phase as the immediate mediator of the transient CC3-width contrast; the prior cause of the foreground phase remains open. Test: VariantTraceTests.test_s88_phase_cell_pair_reproduces_adc3_sweep_at_1500_rpm.
tables.rpm1500_adc3_latch_path: In the 1500-RPM ADC3 step, the G/S88 modeled CC3 pulse beginning at tick 923127 has widths 4901/4765 ticks. Original G publishes IRAM63h=2Dh at tick 903126, whereas S88 publishes it at 923594, after CC3 entry at 923099. S88 and G supplied with ROM7580h=25h use IRAM14h:15h=04AAh at that entry; native G uses 04CCh. The raw 34-unit difference corresponds to the 136-tick width difference in the emulator. Code at 4629h, 4752h..4762h, 1D4Bh, 1ED3h and 058Eh is byte-identical across G/S88. This shows timing of the modeled sensor-state publication mediates this transient; the upstream path change and physical output remain unresolved. Test: VariantTraceTests.test_s88_phase_cell_pair_reproduces_adc3_sweep_at_1500_rpm.
tables.rpm3000_sweep_s88_replication: At 3000 RPM, native G and S88 matched 427/456 modeled CC3 edges with maximum four-tick delta. Supplying S88 ROM7580h=25h only at G MOVC PC5289h matched 435/456; adding S88 ROM7B45h=0Dh matched 456/456. At this RPM the effect is small and conditional; no physical actuator or scale follows from these traces. Test: VariantTraceTests.test_s88_phase_cell_pair_reproduces_adc3_sweep_at_3000_rpm.
tables.rpm1500_sweep_s88_replication: At 1500 RPM in the same Fiat harness, G matched 215/226 S88 modeled CC3 edges; S88 ROM7580h=25h delivered only at G MOVC PC5289h matched 221/226 and removed the largest 136-tick transient mismatch. Test: VariantTraceTests.test_s88_phase_cell_pair_reproduces_adc3_sweep_at_1500_rpm.
tables.coolant_sweep_s88_factorial: Original G ROM7580h=10h and S88=25h are each read 308 times by MOVC PC5289h during matched 3.2M-tick 1000-RPM ADC3 sweeps. Of 203 modeled CC3 events, native G matches S88 at only 10 tick/level pairs. Supplying S88's 25h only at the G MOVC result matches 198 pairs; also supplying S88's 7B45h=0Dh matches all 203, PC coverage and the 195052 MOVC reads and per-window address counts. Original G ROM bytes and raw MOVC records are unchanged. This establishes a dominant digital phase contribution in this tested Fiat harness state, not a physical RPM scale or ECU output identity. tables.static_evidence: The two code families have identical MOVC state-selection opcodes at offsets 4CA0h and 4D63h; their branch targets relocate. Bytes 7290h:7291h are 46h:85h in all six. G/S88 7292h..7294h are 89h:13h:BCh, versus 04h:94h:38h in A/A+/S37/S36. Byte 7294h is independently used as index zero of the matrix threshold block 7294h..7299h.
tables.dynamic_evidence: Isolated execution of each original ROM with prepared serial states 2, 3 and 4 stages its own 7292h, 7293h and 7294h values in IRAM45h, then the original MOV S0BUF,45h instruction sends each value to the emulated serial register. In full G and S88 emulator boots at 1000 RPM, SIGUSR1 5-baud stimulus and no scanner peer, both write 55h 46h 85h 89h 13h BCh to the PTY, then repeat while unanswered. The PTY writes return 1 and original ROM hashes remain unchanged. The Fiat G run_test.sh client now reads Key5=BCh explicitly, responds with ~Key2=7Ah, receives identification packets and completes the handshake. This is a modeled Fiat result, not a physical ECU wire capture or the A-family full-boot path.
tables.scanner_evidence: The reference scanner ECUMonomotronic.cpp handshake reads only four key bytes after 55h and comments key4 as BCh. The original G/S88 ROM contains five candidate state bytes 46h 85h 89h 13h BCh; the repo BOSCH_MONOMOTRONIC_PROTOCOL.md notes this five-byte possibility. These source comments do not prove which bytes were received on physical hardware.

tables.static_evidence: MOV A,R5; ADD A,#94h; MOVC A,@A+DPTR reads 7294h+R5. CJNE A,B compares threshold to R3, and if threshold>=R3 with other guards clear, 1480h..1484h assigns R2=0,R3=threshold. Equality also discards a nonzero fractional R2, so this is not a strict numeric floor on R3:R2. Only the first byte differs between code families; the consumer bytes are identical after relocation.
tables.dynamic_evidence: G at 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=120/95 and ADC7=63: PC1461h reads raw 7298h=AFh 229 times and yields R3:R2=AF00h at PC14C2h, final RAM48h=40h, median RAM14h:15h=1422. Supplying 00h/50h/C0h only at this MOVC gives R3:R2=37C0h/5000h/C000h, RAM48h=14h/1Dh/46h and medians 499/687/1554. The original ROM SHA-256 stays unchanged. With ADC0/6=40/95, the RAM28h.1 path is bypassed and this MOVC is absent.
tables.isolated_revision_evidence: Executing the original 41-byte consumer in all six ROMs with synthetic R5=0 and R3=20h replaces R3:R2 with BC00h in G/S88 or 3800h in A/A+/S37/S36. R5=4 gives AF00h in all six. With R3 exactly equal to the threshold and R2=C0h, all six still zero R2. Natural R5=0 reachability is not established.
tables.natural_index_scan: G/S88 stable ADC0/6=120/95 and 180/247, plus G ADC0 steps 40->120 and 120->40 with ADC6=95, all at 1000 RPM, ADC7=63, 2.4M ticks: whenever PC145Eh was reached, R5=4 and PC1461h read 7298h. No 7294h read was observed. RAM27h.7 was clear at every logged 145Eh passage in the step traces, so the 141Ah branch to 1427h was not taken. PC19A6h sets this bit conditionally; absence in these runs does not prove index 0 unreachable.
tables.index_0_control_flow: G 1396h loads R4/R5 from XRAM A6h/A5h. The 80-byte G 1412h..1461h branch is byte-identical in S88 and A-family code at +4Eh. With T2I1=0, IRAM2Ch.5=0, IRAM27h.7=1, R4=5 and R5=0, this branch preserves R5=0 and reads ROM7294h=BCh in G/S88 or 38h in A/A+/S37/S36. With R4=4, it changes R5 to 4 and reads ROM7298h=AFh in all six. Original-ROM opcode tests confirm both cases. G 1396h..1411h and A shifted upstream code differ only in a relocated LJMP target byte. Natural coexistence of the prerequisite state and guards remains unverified, and A-family full-emulator hardware compatibility is unproven.
tables.state_write_provenance: In current 12M-tick G/S88 ADC5-cycle runs, optional changed-value tracing of external XRAM F8:A5h records autotest PC55A1h writing 00->55->AA, cleanup PC0A51h writing AA->00, and matrix state persistence PC14B9h writing 00->04 then later values 1..5. Original G 1396h reads this XRAM byte into R5 via MOVX, distinct from upper IRAM @A5h accessed elsewhere. These are observed value-changing writes only; equal-value writes and other pointer paths are not ruled out. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/matrix_state_writes_adc5_cycle_g/; slow G/S88 regression confirms all three PCs.
tables.natural_indices_3_and_5: G/S88 at 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=120/95, ADC3=4, ADC7=63 and ADC5=40/200: PC19A6h/19ACh naturally sets RAM27h.7/.6 after PSW.1=1 with R7=40h/A6h; PC1461h then reads 7299h=E9h at R5=5 (42 reads each) or 7297h=68h at R5=3 (13 G/11 S88 reads). Supplying 00h only at that specific MOVC, while keeping original ROM hashes, changes final RAM48h G/S88 from 56h to 14h/18h for ADC5=40 and from 26h to 14h/18h for ADC5=200. Post-transition median IRAM14h:15h changes G/S88 1566.5->424/489.5 for ADC5=40 and 669/673.5->389.5/451 for ADC5=200. Times are emulated ticks, and the physical ADC5 scale and actuator identity are unverified.
tables.extended_natural_index_scan: G/S88 at 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=120/95, ADC3=4, ADC7=63, ADC5 initial 10-bit 160 and steps 2400000:800,4800000:160,7200000:800,9600000:160 over 12M ticks: PC1461h naturally reads all addresses 7295h..7299h, corresponding to R5=1..5. The original hashes are retained. Transition-only PC1412h trace in build/ma17-analysis/variants/matrix_pre_adc5_cycle_{g,s88}/ records initial R4=0,R5=0,RAM27=04h,RAM2C=28h,T2CON=85h, so RAM2C.5 bypasses the index-zero path. Later RAM27.7=1 and RAM2C.5=0 are observed, but recorded R5 is 1..5 and R4 reaches at most 2; no state combines R4=5,R5=0,RAM27.7=1,RAM2C.5=0,T2I1=0. A 22M-tick eight-step repetition also reaches indices 1..5 without reading 7294h. A G constant-ADC5=40 12M-tick control reached 1..5 too. No claim is made that R5=0 is unreachable in other operating states.
tables.modeled_pin_effect: In the same post-transition windows, modeled CC3/P1.3 median low widths change 6225->1685 ticks (G ADC5=40), 6224->1946 (S88 40), 2665->1547 (G 200), and 2682->1792 (S88 200) when only the selected MOVC result is supplied as 00h. tables.direction_flag_consumer: Original identical bytes at G/S88 199Eh..19B5h and A-family 19BAh..19D1h: PSW.1=0 clears RAM27h.6/.7; with PSW.1=1, R7 sign selects .7 for nonnegative and .6 for negative. Isolated original-opcode tests verify all three branches in six ROMs. A 16-state G grid varying TPS, ADC2, ADC3 and RPM but leaving ADC5 at default reached PC199Eh 54 times per state without PSW.1 or PC19A6h; this is negative evidence only for those states.
tables.flag_source_evidence: G at ADC0/6=120/95: PC10F3h..1104h compares RAM66h=5Fh minus 5 with RAM60h=78h, sets carry and B.4, PC113Ch aggregates B.4 into RAM28h.1, and PC115Eh writes 10h to XRAM F889h. At 40/95, RAM60h=28h, carry and B.4 stay zero and F889h is not set. These are emulated digital states, not calibrated TPS angles.
tables.tps_state_history_evidence: G 1000 RPM, ADC3=4, ADC5=200, ADC7=63: starting ADC0/6=120/95 sets F889h=10h at PC115Eh/tick58299, while starting at 180/247 leaves F889h=00h after RAM self-test. Stepping the former to 180/247 at tick1200000 updates raw RAM60h/66h to B4h/F7h, but B.4 remains 1 at 1132h and RAM28h.1/.2 remain set; the direct-high case has the same raw pair with B.4=0 and RAM28h=00h. Isolated original opcodes 10B1h..115Eh with R2=B4h,R4=F7h and prior RAM28h=06h show B=00h clears .1/.2, B=10h retains both. Physical TPS angle and lambda mode remain unverified.
tables.tps_fault_context: G RAM28h.1/.2 have isolated original-opcode paths through XRAM F885h/F84Fh to fault-table triplets 02 06 1D and 02 06 1E; a PTY session with ADC0/6=120/95 transmitted 02 06 1B. All encode scanner fault code 0602h with different status bytes. Thus the 120/95 calibration experiments may exercise TPS-fault behavior; normal-operation fuel calibration must be checked at a pair with these flags clear.

tables.tps_release_cc3_effect: Original G at 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=180/247, ADC3/5/7=34/110/63, with ADC0/6 stepped to 40/95 at tick 3274600, reads 7895h 3160 times and never reads 78BDh in 4M ticks. Donating only A's 7895h MOVC bytes preserves active G ROM hash, changes F8:01h 72h->9Ah, and produces 69 of 386 1CB7h consumer visits with nonzero IRAM7Ah in both arms. Among 129 CC3 scheduler entries, zero IRAM14h:15h intervals after the step rise from 2 to 14, and modeled CC3 pin low starts fall from 127 to 115 while the global median width remains 4404 ticks. At scheduler entry 107, control candidate R3:R2=00CAh crosses the ROM 00C8h bound and is published, whereas donor candidate 0044h stays below it and is cleared; donor first publishes 00D5h at entry 119. P5 median width remains 1921 ticks. This establishes a causal pulse-count effect in the emulated G model, not physical injector identity or natural A-code reachability.

tables.dynamic_evidence: At G 1000 RPM, ADC0/6=40/95 and ADC3/5/7=4/200/63, the natural 3E1Ah branch occurs 369 times and reads 78BDh 1736 times in 2.4M ticks. Donating only A's 20 MOVC bytes to the intact G ROM changes the last 3E33h accumulator and later XRAM F8:01h from 72h to 9Ah; the G firmware SHA-256 remains unchanged. In this state IRAM7Ah=00h and modeled P5/CC3 median widths remain 1861/2372 ticks. With ADC5=40 the same run selects 7895h instead (1940 reads, zero 78BDh reads). A second G run starts with ADC0/6=180/247, ADC3/5/7=4/200/63 and steps ADC0/6 to 40/95 at tick 3274600. It reads 78BDh 2988 times; 69 of 386 1CB7h consumer visits have nonzero IRAM7Ah. In the final visit IRAM7Ah=8Ch and donating A cells changes F8:01h 72h->9Ah and the calculated B at 1CDFh 0Ch->10h. Modeled P5/CC3 median widths remain 1921/4464 ticks. This proves conditional digital propagation through the original multiply chain, not a physical actuator effect.
tables.late_cc3_effect: In the TPS-step run, the global CC3 median width conceals a changed event sequence. At instruction tick 3296198, original G code has R3:R2=00E2h (control) or 005Ah (A-cell donor) at 1EA9h. ROM[DPTR+18h:19h] supplies comparison bound 00C8h. The donor candidate is below the bound; with XRAM F8:08h=61h (sign clear) and F8:EFh=00h, 1EB9h..1EC7h clears R5:R4 and 1ECBh..1ED3h publishes IRAM14h:15h=0000h. Control skips this clear and publishes 00E2h. Original G code visits the CC3 scheduler 129 times in both arms; with A's 78BDh cells donated, IRAM14h:15h is 0000h in 10 consecutive visits (instruction indices 3315115..3582432), versus nonzero in control. Modeled CC3 pin low starts fall from 129 to 119. Subsequent nonzero scheduled widths also differ. This is causal in the emulated CC3/P1.3 model; the physical circuit destination is not verified.
tables.isolated_six_rom_evidence: Original G/S88 opcodes at 3E14h..3E33h and A/A+/S37/S36 opcodes at 3ED1h..3EF0h select 7080h or 7084h according to 2Ch.4 with 2Fh.1=0 and T2I1=0. With R5=2 and zero interpolation fractions, the selected row-zero column-two byte is written through MOVX @R1 to F8:01h: G/S88/S37/S36 give 80h (7895h) or 81h (78BDh); A/A+ give A8h or A9h. This proves code and pointer homology in an isolated prepared state, not natural A-code boot reachability.
tables.six_rom_bound_gate: Code alignment maps G 1CB7h/1EA9h/1ED3h to A-code 1CD3h/1EC5h/1EEFh. Original opcodes and ROM[7218h:7219h]=00C8h are identical across all six images at the bound comparison and publication. In isolated prepared executions, candidate 005Ah publishes 0000h when F8:08h=61h and F8:EFh=00h; the same candidate publishes 00C8h if F8:08h has bit 7 set or F8:EFh=01h with 2Fh.0 set. F8:EFh=01h with 2Fh.0 clear still publishes 0000h. Candidate 00E2h publishes 00E2h. This verifies the gate's original six-ROM behavior, not natural A-code entry conditions.
tables.boundary_evidence: Original six-ROM opcodes with R5=15, R0=4, R4=80h and R6=0 read 78D1h=00h at MOVC 5350h/5413h while DPTR remains 78BDh. With original 1386h producer and 3329h->3384h reader under prepared guards, raw RAM47h=40 selects index 3 and R2=99h in A, versus index 5 and R2=8Eh in S37 when RAM2Bh.7=0. With the flag set, both constant 7EACh banks yield R2=99h. Identical table bytes therefore do not imply identical output for the same raw digital input; physical input scaling and natural flag selection remain unknown. Test: Sab80C517.AlcoholCodeAdc3StateLadderSelectsDifferentMatrixCell.
tables.full_raw_transfer_evidence: Original A/S37 opcodes 1386h and 3329h->3384h were executed for all 256 raw RAM47h values with prepared guards, twice per input for RAM2Bh.7=0/1. The identical 7E9Dh bytes produce different R2 values for 215 inputs, first at 22 and last at 236; both 7EACh banks produce constant 99h for all 256 inputs. The effect is caused by different 7570h segment axes, not different curve bytes. Reproducible CSV/PNG/JSON: build/ma17-analysis/variants/matrix_plots/curve_7e9d_a_s37_transfer.*; plot command: /usr/bin/python3 tools/plot_ma17_curve_transfer.py <CSV>. This is a digital prepared-state transfer, not a physical scale or natural mode selection. Test: Sab80C517.AlcoholCodeAdc3StateLadderSelectsDifferentMatrixCell.
tables.a_s37_code_window_alignment: Original A and S37 bytes are identical in windows 01ABh..01BFh, 0DD2h..0E04h, 0E35h..0EAFh, 1386h..139Dh, 3329h..3332h, 3384h..33D2h, 533Ch..538Ch and 53E4h..540Bh. These cover RAM47h copy/write, segment lookup, bank selection and interpolation in the tested path; 7570h segment increments differ. This supports the raw digital axis attribution but does not equate physical RPM scaling or ECU hardware. Test: CurveTransferTests.test_a_s37_producer_and_reader_code_windows_match.
tables.a_s37_horizontal_translation: All fourteen nonzero 7570h raw RAM47h segment starts in S37 are exactly 20 counts below A. The original-opcode prepared-state sweep confirms R2_S37(x, default bank) = R2_A(x+20, default bank) for every x=0..235 (236 comparisons, zero mismatches). The initial 0..4 interval also matches because both curves begin with a 99h plateau. This is a digital input translation; it does not establish an RPM conversion or equivalent hardware clocks. Test: Sab80C517.AlcoholCodeAdc3StateLadderSelectsDifferentMatrixCell; reproducible metrics: curve_7e9d_a_s37_transfer.json.
tables.isolated_A_code_evidence: Original A/A+/S37/S36 opcodes from 3384h to 33D3h, with R7=4 derived from upper IRAM BCh, R6 zeroed and T2CON.1=0: RAM2Bh.7=0 reaches MOVC at 53F2h with DPTR=7E9Dh and writes ROM[7EA1h]=94h to R2 and upper A4h; flag=1 reaches DPTR=7EACh and writes ROM[7EB0h]=99h. This proves branch behavior, not natural flag reachability.
tables.index_boundary_evidence: In all four A-code ROMs, original 3329h..3332h opcodes split prepared upper IRAM BCh=A0h|index into R7=index and R6=A0h. With R6 zeroed for exact-cell lookup and the 3384h guard prepared, indices 0 and 3 return 99h from both 7E9Dh and 7EACh; index 4 returns 94h versus 99h and index 13 returns 2Bh versus 99h. This proves the raw-bank divergence at the fourth/fifth-cell boundary under isolated execution, not a physical axis scale. Test: Sab80C517.AlcoholCodeFlagSelectsConstant7eacCurve.
tables.digital_axis_evidence: In the integrated original-opcode A/S37 test, both ROMs have 7046h->7570h and header ROM7570h=47h. The A 1386h producer segments RAM47h and writes upper BCh. Sweeping every raw RAM47h byte 0..255 matched the column predicted by cumulative ROM7572h..7580h increments in both A and S37 (512 comparisons); 3329h then copies BCh low nibble into R7. The group-specific start lists are stored separately; G/A/A+ and S88/S37/S36 lists are calculated from their original ROMs and checked by MatrixPlotTests.test_7eac_raw_ram47_axis_differs_between_a_and_s37. This proves the A/S37 digital index mapping under prepared state, not a physical RPM conversion or natural selector frequency. Test: Sab80C517.AlcoholCodeAdc3StateLadderSelectsDifferentMatrixCell.
tables.integrated_A_code_evidence: A and S37 original opcodes in one CPU instance process upper A8h/A9h=60h to RAM63h=60h, enter XRAM F9:85h state 1, and advance prepared counters through states 2, 3 and 4 at PC3C7Dh..3D04h with RAM47h=55h, setting RAM2Bh.7. After the 1378h..13CBh matrix path, the flag remains set. Preparing the separate 3384h reader guard and index 4 reaches PC53F2h with DPTR=7EACh and publishes 99h to R2 and upper A4h. This connects original-code producer and reader under prepared state, not timed full-boot reachability.

tables.format: u8 IRAM address, u8 count=07h, seven cumulative u8 increments; final increment differs by code family
tables.consumer: G 3AADh calls 5279h; A-family 3ADBh calls 533Ch. Both load big-endian pointer 70C4h->7F8Dh and return segment index R3; their following branch compares R3 with upper IRAM83h before indexing the direct 7F96h curve
tables.output: R3 and upper IRAM83h in the visible code path; 7F96h result is combined into upper IRAM8Ch, then bounded before lower IRAM69h. RAM69h feeds the G Timer 1 reload calculation. Natural output effect and physical meaning unknown
tables.static_evidence: All six directory words at 70C4h are 7F8Dh. G/S88/S37/S36 segment header selects lower IRAM0Fh and ends E0h; A/A+ selects lower IRAM35h and ends FFh. The remaining seven curve bytes at 7F96h..7F9Ch are identical. These two changed segment bytes were previously omitted from pointer_regions.json because no higher pointer follows 7F8Dh; the generated terminal candidate now extends provisionally to ROM end, including filler and metadata, while this curated entry stops at 7F96h.
tables.isolated_evidence: Original G code from 3AADh to 3AB3h changes R3 when lower IRAM0Fh changes 00h->80h, but not when 35h changes. Original A code from 3ADBh to 3AE1h changes R3 when lower IRAM35h changes 00h->80h, but not when 0Fh changes. The segment-decoder opcodes G 527Ch..52C8h and A 533Fh..538Bh are byte-identical. With equal values supplied to both candidate IRAM inputs, the 256-value isolated sweep finds different R3 exactly for inputs 00h..1Fh (32 values) and identical R3 for 20h..FFh, consistent with the E0h/FFh final segment increment. This establishes an isolated decoder boundary, not a natural output effect.
tables.conditional_downstream_evidence: Original G opcodes 3AADh..3B07h and A opcodes 3ADBh..3B35h were executed in isolation with upper IRAM8Ch=80h and upper 82h=01h. With initial upper 83h=00h, both ROMs discard changed R3 and produce the same lower 69h. With initial upper 83h=07h, changing the header-selected input changes upper 83h, upper 8Ch and lower 69h; changing the other candidate IRAM byte does not. Supplying 00h equally to lower 0Fh and 35h yields lower 69h=7Fh in G versus 7Ah in A; supplying 20h equally yields 77h in both. The 91-byte consumer paths are identical apart from the relocated decoder-call address, and the decoder bodies are byte-identical, so the equal-source contrast isolates the E0h/FFh final increment in this controlled state. This proves a conditional digital effect, not a naturally reached state or physical P5 effect.
tables.isolated_timer1_consequence: Feeding the two isolated outcomes 69h=7Fh/7Ah into original G code 043Bh..0521h with 31h=59h and 36h:37h=011Dh yields calculated Timer 1 reload pair 34h:35h=4CFEh/34FFh. The IEX3 service later loads this pair into TL1/TH1 at 0286h. This is a chained controlled calculation, not a natural A-ROM run or measured P5 waveform.
tables.controlled_p5_consequence: In three full G-emulator runs at 1000 RPM, raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63 and 2.4M ticks, a pre-043Bh IRAM69h intervention after RPM exists supplied 7Fh or 7Ah while leaving the original G ROM SHA unchanged. Modeled P5.0/P5.1 median low widths were 1921/1863 ticks versus 1861 control; their median periods remained 59400 ticks and CC3 median width remained 3041 ticks. The 7Fh-versus-7Ah modeled P5 contrast is 58 ticks. This intervention bypasses natural 7F8Dh lookup and does not prove that the G or A ROM reaches the isolated state or that P5 is a physical coil pin. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f8d_ram69_{control,7f,7a}_g/.
tables.controlled_full_decoder_consequence: The generic MA17_OVERRIDE_MOVC_AT now accepts comma-separated PC:ADDRESS:VALUE entries. In full G runs at 1000 RPM and raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63, supplying 28h for the MOVC at PC527Dh/7F8Dh makes the decoder read lower IRAM28h=00h. Supplying FFh additionally at PC5289h/7F95h changes R3 after the call from 00h/00h to 05h/05h and upper83h from 00h/00h to 00h/01h on the two visits. Both runs finish lower69h=9Ah with modeled P5.0 median low width 1861 ticks; their full event timing and P5 width histograms differ. These are simultaneous controlled MOVC-return interventions with the original G ROM SHA unchanged, not natural A behavior or a claim that all outputs are identical. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f8d_source28*_g/.
tables.natural_G_access: Original G at 1000 RPM, raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63 and 2.4M ticks makes two MOVC reads each of 7F8Dh=0Fh, 7F8Eh=07h and 7F95h=E0h through pointer 70C4h. The following PC3AD2h reads 7F97h and 7F98h once each, with upper 83h=01h/02h and upper 8Ch=9Ch/9Bh before that instruction. These are natural G-emulator accesses; they do not isolate the terminal segment's contribution to 69h or establish behavior in the A hardware profile. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f8d_natural_g_tps40/.
tables.natural_G_access_matrix: With other raw ADC channels fixed at 130/100/80/90/110/95/63, no K-Line injection, immediate crank and 2.4M ticks, original G visits PC3AAD/3AB3 zero times at 750 RPM/ADC0=4, twice at 1000 RPM/ADC0=4 and 1000 RPM/ADC0=20, and zero times at 1000 RPM/ADC0=200. At 750 RPM/ADC0=4 all 56 PC3A04h samples had R2=upper8Ch=9Ch, so the JNZ path to 3A1Eh/3A67h was not taken; at 1000 RPM/ADC0=4 two samples had R2=9Ah below upper8Ch=9Ch/9Bh. PC3A7Dh saw B=07h twice in each 1000-RPM/ADC0=4 or 20 case, and B=0Fh once with ADC0=200. In that last case B.3=1 takes the direct bypass at 3A80h. At both visited 1000-RPM cases RAM0F=FEh/FFh and R3=06h/06h. This does not establish physical TPS interpretation. Test: VariantTraceTests.test_terminal_segment_access_depends_on_rpm_and_adc0_state_in_g.
tables.natural_G_gate_source: Original G 333Bh/333Fh selects carry from lower IRAM28h.1/.2 using 2Eh.6, and 3341h copies carry to B.3 before storing B in upper IRAM94h. At PC3A04h the same upper94h is loaded into B; PC3A80h tests B.3. In the 1000-RPM/ADC0=4 and 20 traces, the nearest earlier PC3341h event had 2Eh=84h, 28h=00h, carry=0 and upper94h=07h; the subsequent gate saw B=07h. At ADC0=200 the nearest event had 2Eh=84h, 28h=06h, carry=1 and upper94h=0Fh; the gate saw B=0Fh and bypassed the lookup. Code 1132h..1146h is a known producer of 28h.1/.2 in the two-track input routine, but these raw ADC pairs and the physical sensor interpretation are not validated.
tables.natural_G_masking_experiment: With the same G 1000-RPM ADC state on emulator SHA-256 e2a3e9fe89c35ce3b451af75e9ce8af4ed616ade528e601b3cc94130c2a65ac5, trace at PC3AAD saw lower IRAM0Fh=FEh/FFh and 35h=FFh on the two visits; PC3AB3 returned R3=06h both times. Supplying A's 35h only at MOVC PC527Dh/7F8Dh, or A's FFh only at PC5289h/7F95h, each left R3, structured RAM/lookup/CC3/P5/PC-coverage observations and final RAM69h=9Ah unchanged. Both overrides were logged and the active G ROM SHA remained original. This is masking in one natural G state, not proof that either A calibration byte is globally inactive or that A hardware behaves like G. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f8d_factorial/.
tables.natural_G_rpm_sweep: Original G at raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63, immediate crank, no K-Line and 2.4M ticks visited PC3AAD 6/8/11/15 times at 1500/2000/3000/4000 RPM. Observed lower IRAM0Fh ranges were F2h..FDh, E3h..FDh, C3h..F9h and A4h..FEh respectively; PC3AB3 returned R3=06h on every visit. Extending the 4000-RPM run to 4M ticks still yielded exactly 15 visits, the last at tick=308113 with IRAM0Fh=FEh. On 362 later visits to PC3A04h, R2=upper IRAM8Ch=40h, so the SUBB at 3A0Eh produces zero and JNZ at 3A10h does not enter the decoder. The isolated differential input range 00h..1Fh was not reached in these states. Captures: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f8d_natural_g_rpm{1500,2000,3000,4000}/, terminal_7f8d_natural_g_rpm4000_long/ and terminal_7f8d_natural_g_rpm4000_long_ram69/.

Determine whether natural operation reaches equal-source inputs 00h..1Fh or different-source combinations that change R3

tables.format: seven raw u8 values indexed by upper IRAM83h; the 3AADh/3ADBh path bounds the index to 0..6

axes.source: upper IRAM[83h]

tables.consumer: G 3ACEh..3AD2h uses DPTR=7F96h; homologous A-code 3AFCh..3B00h
tables.output: negated lookup value conditionally added to upper IRAM8Ch; subsequent G 3AF1h..3B06h bounds and writes lower IRAM69h
tables.static_evidence: All six ROMs have identical seven bytes immediately after the 7F8Dh segment header and increments. In the G 3AADh path and homologous A 3ADBh path, the table count is 07h; the decoder returns R3 in 0..6, and the comparison either assigns R3 to upper IRAM83h, retains a smaller value, or increments that smaller value by one. Thus the MOVC with DPTR=7F96h uses an index in 0..6 on this path. Earlier branches jump to the same MOVC with a different DPTR. This curve has no dedicated pointer-directory slot.
tables.dynamic_evidence: A current original G trace at 1000 RPM and raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63 reads 7F97h=01h and 7F98h=03h once each at PC3AD2h over 2.4M ticks. Upper 83h=01h/02h and upper 8Ch=9Ch/9Bh immediately before the respective MOVC instructions. A prior trace observed one read of 7F96h=01h in another state. This establishes natural G access, not a frequency estimate or isolated output contribution.
tables.conditional_downstream_evidence: In isolated original G/A code with upper 8Ch=80h, changing the header-selected input changes lower 69h only when initial upper 83h=07h; initial 83h=00h masks the change. The tested branch uses the direct 7F96h curve. This is conditional digital mediation, not observed natural ECU output behavior.
tables.natural_G_movc_causality: At 1000 RPM, raw ADC0..7=40/130/100/80/90/110/95/63, immediate crank and 2.4M ticks, original G reads 7F97h=01h then 7F98h=03h at PC3AD2h. Native execution writes lower 69h via PC3B06h as 9Ch->9Bh->9Ah. Supplying 00h only at those two MOVC addresses leaves 69h at 9Ch until a later direct 9Ah write; supplying FFh makes the first read write 9Ah and suppresses the second visit. The immediate upper 8Ch values after the first read are respectively 9Bh/9Ch/9Ah for native/00h/FFh. All active ROM hashes equal original G, and P5.0 median low width remains 1861 ticks in all three runs; event timing and histories differ. This establishes a naturally reached digital contribution to transient lower 69h in the G emulator state, not a physical output effect or full-state equivalence. Capture: build/ma17-analysis/variants/terminal_7f96_movc/; test: VariantTraceTests.test_terminal_7f96_movc_changes_natural_ram69_history.

tables.format: raw bytes in terminal pointer candidate; no table structure or consumer established
tables.static_evidence: No directory slot begins in this interval. G/A/A+ have 87 FFh bytes plus common 07h and 45h at 7FF3h/7FF4h; S37/S36 change 81 earlier FFh bytes to 00h, while S88 has a different 74-byte pattern. The immediately preceding 7F96h curve cannot read into this interval via the G 3AADh / A 3ADBh segment path: its MOVC index is bounded to 0..6. This does not exclude other indirect readers. The following ten bytes at 7FF6h belong to a separate boot-copy block.
tables.dynamic_evidence: G/S88 2.4M-tick traces in experiments_opcode86_fixed/gate63_tps_40_95/ observed no MOVC reads from 7F9Dh..7FEFh. This is one tested trajectory, not proof of global inaccessibility.
open_questions: Find whether any indirect ROM read reaches this interval
Determine whether variant patterns are filler, identification or functional data

tables.format: ten positional u8 initialization bytes copied to XRAM F8 page
tables.consumer: Six-ROM original boot code copies 7FF6h..7FFFh by MOVC/MOVX before PC0B30h; G/S88 4A31h..4A7Eh and A-family 4AF4h..4B41h later compare the final nine copied bytes against ROM
tables.output: XRAM F8:0Fh,1Eh,49h,4Ah,63h,64h,3Fh,4Dh,8Fh,DEh in ROM order; physical roles unknown
tables.static_evidence: No pointer-directory slot begins here. The six differing offsets are 7FF6h,7FF7h,7FFCh..7FFFh; four middle bytes are identical in all ROMs. The nine-byte later integrity comparison excludes 7FF6h.
tables.dynamic_evidence: Sab80C517.SixRomXramSelfTestReachesCommonBootContinuation executes original opcodes and confirms all ten per-ROM copies to the listed F8 destinations. Sab80C517.SixRomTailBytesGuardXramIntegrity exercises the later nine-byte comparison and its guarded restart behavior in isolation.
tables.full_boot_trace_evidence: Original G and S88 at 1000 RPM, ADC0/2/3/5/6/7=40/220/80/40/95/63 and 2.4M ticks: optional MA17_TRACE_BOOT_XRAM_FIELDS logged all ten PC0AABh copies with values equal to the active ROM 7FF6h..7FFFh, then nine PC5896h reads equal to the copied values. F8:0Fh was excluded from that guard. Among the six fields changed between G and A, no other read PC was observed after excluding XRAM self-test PC55A2h and pre-copy PC092Eh for F8:1Eh. Repeating G at 4000 RPM and ADC0/3/6=180/232/247 produced the same set of reader PCs for these ten fields. G 1000-RPM trace-on/off execution.json objects for output latches, CC3, engine RAM and PC coverage are identical. This bounds the observed behavior only in these G/S88 states; A-family full boot was not exercised.
open_questions: Identify the later uses of each initialized F8 field
Determine whether the four common ASCII-like bytes have an intentional identifier role
